content:
Rick Springfield claims he killed a man while touring for the US military in Vietnam during the late 1960s.

The Australian musician recounted the shocking story during an appearance on this week's Joe Rogan Experience.

Speaking on the podcast, the 'Jessie's Girl' singer said: 'You could actually tour during the war in Vietnam – it was insane. We were there for about four months. I thought, "This is great, I'm going to make some money." You know? But of course, we didn't make any money.'

At one point, the focus of the tour shifted from earning money to simply staying alive, as the band was attacked while living alongside soldiers.

Springfield recalled: 'It was like a movie. On the radio, they're saying, "We've got movement here. Identify if friendlies." And they go, "No, there are no friendlies here." And the radio says, "You want a few mortar rounds down?" And I'm like, "Okay, let's go." It was like a John Wayne moment. I was just a kid. I had no idea what I was doing. I said, "Yeah, let's shoot."'

He added: 'I dropped mortars down the tube, like five or six of them. I mean, I could have blown my hands off at any time.' The next morning, someone came to tell him that one of the mortar rounds had hit a Viet Cong member.

Springfield, who was just 18 at the time, only then realised the gravity of what he had done by dropping the mortars.

He said: 'The worst thing is that my mortar hit somebody. That's probably the one thing I've brought back that I haven't been able to find a place for.'

When host Joe Rogan asked how long the memory had haunted him, Springfield replied: 'Always.'

He said: 'It's hard for me to face the fact that I ended a life, even though it was in a war far away and I wasn't really a party to it and didn't really know what I was doing.' He added: 'When I think about the weight of it all, it really does get heavy.'
